osaka_iwai_bettei_kitashinchi.notes: [Sushi · Kitashinchi, sushi and tempura in one course] The Kitashinchi branch of Iwai, a group that grew from a tempura and wine restaurant in Ashiya whose Michelin star two years running made its name (official site); here the tempura shares a course with Edo-style sushi. Diners describe a chef who talks diners through each dish and puts nervous first-timers at ease; the tempura is soft rather than crisp, which a June 2026 diner did not care for and a July 2026 diner called a matter of taste. Private rooms for two to six (a December 2025 diner booked one for a business dinner); tell the chef if you are short of time. Service charge 10%.

osaka_sushi_sogoro_kitashinchi.notes: [Sushi · Kitashinchi main street, seven seats] A seven-seat counter on Kitashinchi's main street that began as a standing sushi bar; the sign still said so in December 2024, but everyone sits now. At ¥13,200 for dinner (lunch ¥6,600 or ¥8,800), diners call it remarkably reasonable for Kitashinchi. The chef is friendly and full of jokes, described in a December 2024 review as multilingual. One December 2025 diner felt rushed by sushi piling up; on a return in September 2026 the same diner found the service much improved. Seats are close together. No children below junior-high age; book ahead.

osaka_critters_burger_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Burgers · Amerikamura, a pioneer since 2009] A wood-fronted American burger house in Amerikamura that opened in 2009, before gourmet burgers had caught on in Kansai, and has been in Tabelog's Hamburger 100 seven times since 2017. The bun is the point: made from Hokkaido wheat and natural yeast at the sister bakery, toasted, fluffy inside and firm enough to hold the juicy all-beef patty to the last bite. Order the double cheeseburger (¥2,365 in October 2026), or the spinach bacon burger, the house favourite since at least 2018. Expect a few groups waiting at the 11:00 opening and many overseas visitors; evening tables can be booked from 18:00. Note that smoking is allowed from 17:00.

roles: Representative of CRITTERS BURGER (Kansai Walker 2018)
chef_bio.background: Per Kansai Walker (2018): the representative 栗田宗太朗 went to an international school hoping to study at an American university, then trained at an architecture college, qualified as an architect and worked three or four years as a site supervisor for a housebuilder. The father, a programmer, baked bread as a hobby and opened a bakery near the family home, baking every morning while the mother sold the bread; the younger brother, three years younger, came in to help. The brothers decided to make burgers with that bread, ran a mobile stall for about a year around 淀屋橋 and at festivals, and opened the shop in Shinsaibashi, an area known since high school, in 2009 with 20 burgers on the menu. The first two years were hard and delivery kept the shop going. When the family bakery could no longer keep up with the buns, West Wood Bakers opened in 2013, then The Pie Shop in 2016 (Kansai Walker). Time Out (2025) calls it a pioneer of high-end beef burgers in Osaka. Tabelog Hamburger 100 in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024 and 2026.

osaka_cafe_basara_kaerudo_kitahorie.notes: [Curry café · Kita-Horie by Nishi-Ohashi Stn] A slightly hidden, old-style café a minute from Nishi-Ohashi Station, where the smell of curry reaches the street. The monthly Inaka Gozen of small vegetable dishes is the lighter choice. The owner cooks everything alone, so busy lunches mean a short wait (September 2026). Dogs are welcome on the terrace. Cash only. Tabelog Cafe WEST 100 in 2021, 2022 and 2025.

osaka_ajinoya_honten_namba.hours_raw: Tue–Sun and holidays 11:00–22:00, a full close at 22:00; closed Monday and New Year's Day, and sometimes the last Monday and Tuesday of the month (official site). No same-day bookings and no bookings by phone or email; a TableCheck FastPass buys a timed place at the front of the queue (up to 4 people, valid 15 minutes after the slot, the whole party present, 90 minutes at busy times), and bookings through AutoReserve are void (official site). Founded 1965 (official site).
osaka_ajinoya_honten_namba.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Namba, a queue since 1965] An okonomiyaki house founded in 1965, on a second floor opposite the stage door of the 松竹座 theatre, with a retro interior that the shop itself likens to a trip back to an old downtown okonomiyaki stand. Staff mix, pour, flip and sauce every okonomiyaki on the iron plate at your table; the batter is light, the result fluffy, sweetish sauce on top. Order the Ajinoya Mix, the tomato and cheese, or the Kujo green-onion negiyaki with beef tendon, which October 2026 diners singled out. The queue is the catch: in October 2026 an hour or more at dinner, so register at the terminal outside, walk off and come back on the text message, or buy a FastPass. In Tabelog's Okonomiyaki 100 most years since 2018, it now has two sister shops, 味乃家はなれ and 四代目味乃家, the second opened in July 2026 at the Namba Oriental Hotel.

Sister shops: 味乃家はなれ (reservation only, formerly the 寺田町 central kitchen, 天王寺区) and 四代目味乃家 (opened 31 July 2026 in The Namba Central Eatery, Namba Oriental Hotel 1F). chef_bio.philosophy: "Each one grilled with care, one at a time" (official site, translated).
chef_bio.specialty: Ajinoya Mix okonomiyaki; Kujo green-onion negiyaki with beef tendon; mix yakisoba.

osaka_pesca_shinsaibashi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; the listing asks guests to note allergies in the booking comments. The signature "Paitza" is a pizza on flaky pastry, and pasta, baguette and cakes run through the courses; carpaccio, steak, duck and garlic rice are dishes without obvious wheat, but nothing is stated about their sauces.
osaka_pesca_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. The courses are built on fish, pork, wagyu, duck and cheese; the à la carte menu is long and changes with the market, so ask what can be made without animal products.
osaka_pesca_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Daily 15:00–24:00; closed irregularly (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; note allergies or a dessert plate with a message in the booking comments (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners; PIN needed for IC cards from April 2025) and e-money; no QR payments (Tabelog). 24 seats: about 10 at the counter, a table for four and one for six (September 2026 review); private hire for 20 to 50; non-smoking; BYO drinks possible; no minors (Tabelog). No sign on the ground floor: take the lift to the top, 10th floor and walk to the far end of the outdoor corridor (September 2026 reviews).
osaka_pesca_shinsaibashi.notes: [Italian · Nishi-Shinsaibashi, a 10th-floor hideaway] An Italian restaurant with no sign at street level: take the lift of an apartment-like building on the Amerikamura side to the top floor and walk to the end of the open corridor. Inside are a counter of about ten, two tables and soft light, with one chef at the counter, a cook behind and two people serving (September 2026). Order the carpaccio of three fish, which several 2026 diners singled out, and the "Paitza", a pizza on crisp, flaky pastry, then a pasta, such as mackerel and bottarga or duck and porcini cream. Couples, groups of friends and birthday dinners fill it, and the kitchen will write a message on the dessert plate. Tabelog puts the average at ¥5,000–5,999 a head, and the courses run ¥6,600–8,800; open from 15:00 to midnight. Tabelog Italian 100 in 2021; there is a sister shop in Namba.

osaka_okonomiyaki_dan_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: okonomiyaki filled with pork, beef, squid, shrimp or scallops, a batter with a hint of dashi (September 2026), and grilled chicken and seafood on the side.
osaka_okonomiyaki_dan_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–04:00 (last order 03:30); holidays 17:00–21:00 (last order 20:30); closed Sunday (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, and recommended: an August 2026 diner found every seat booked (Tabelog; August 2026). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 23 seats, no private rooms; non-smoking; takeaway and delivery (Tabelog). On the third floor of a mixed-use building that is easy to miss; one diner warns of street touts outside (October 2026).
osaka_okonomiyaki_dan_shinsaibashi.notes: [Okonomiyaki · Souemoncho, until 4 a.m.] A third-floor okonomiyaki counter in a mixed-use building on the Souemoncho street, easy to miss among the touts below, and open until four in the morning, which makes it a late-night favourite of local drinkers; it was named a Tabelog Okonomiyaki 100 in 2025. The okonomiyaki is fluffy and light, with cabbage that keeps its crunch and a sweetish sauce, and it comes to the teppan in front of you, with room on the counter for a proper plate. Start with grilled squid or plump shrimp with mayonnaise and mustard over a drink, then a pork okonomiyaki (¥950 in October 2026, or ¥1,350 for a double), a beef and egg modern-yaki or the yakisoba omelet one diner rated above everything else. Mains run ¥950–2,100. Book: an August 2026 diner found every seat reserved. Closed Sundays; holidays close at 21:00.

osaka_hong_kong_kaisen_yumcha_shinsaibas.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. Vegetable dishes exist (stir-fried water spinach, bok choy, eggplant, tomato with egg), but the kitchen is built on seafood, pork and chicken, and vegetable plates may use oyster sauce or bacon.

The official site gives dinner to 23:00 (last order 22:30 on weekdays, 22:00 at weekends and holidays) and occasional closures. Lunch menu and prices are the same at weekends (official site; August 2026). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). Service charge 3% (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay and others); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 110 seats, private rooms for 6, 8 and 10–20, whole-floor hire for 50 or more; non-smoking with a smoking area outside; children welcome with high chairs, strollers welcome (Tabelog). Step-free from the entrance, wheelchairs can reach the tables (official site); the lift opens straight into the restaurant (August 2026). One hour free at the partner car park with ¥5,000 spent (official site).
osaka_hong_kong_kaisen_yumcha_shinsaibas.notes: [Chinese · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, dim sum and a live tank] A large Hong Kong-style dining room up a lift above a 7-Eleven, with a tank of live sea bream, abalone and kuruma prawns at the door and round tables for groups; named a Tabelog Chinese WEST 100 in 2021. The dim sum is made by a chef holding China's special-grade dim sum master qualification, the wrappers in house, and the tank fish is cooked as you choose, including a Chinese-style sashimi dressed with soy, sesame and cashews. Lunch is the bargain: weekly sets from ¥850 with free rice and soup (a ¥1,000 pork and vegetable set came with gyoza, tofu and almond jelly in August 2026), or dim sum courses from ¥1,950 for two. Evenings lean to banquets: about ¥6,000–7,000 for a course with all-you-can-drink. Diners in 2026 praised the gentle spice and the homemade dim sum wrappers, while one found the staff blunt (September 2026) and another was unimpressed in a near-empty room (October 2026). Add 3% service. The company also runs a branch in Umeda and a hotel in Shima.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the dim sum is made by a 特級点心師, a Chinese national qualification for cooks with eight grades taken one at a time in exams held every two years, so that it takes at least fifteen years to reach; the chef has more than twenty years of cooking. Seafood bought from the market goes live into the tank and is cooked to order. The shop is the 心斎橋本店 of 會通株式会社, which also runs a branch in Umeda (Breeze Breeze 6F) and the 一楽温泉ホテル in Shima, Mie (honkonkaisen.com); Tabelog says seafood comes direct from that hotel. Tabelog Chinese WEST 100, 2021. An August 2026 diner notes the staff are Chinese.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Warm human contact" and "handmade" food, not service bound by a manual (company site).

Reservations accepted; courses are also bookable on Ikyu (April 2026 review). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). 36 seats with counter and sofa seating, two private rooms for 4; non-smoking; takeaway (Tabelog). Moved to Shinmachi in 2003 (Tabelog).
osaka_vrai_de_vrai_chez_hiro_shinmachi.notes: [French · Shinmachi, generous courses on a quiet corner] A calm French restaurant on a back-street corner in Shinmachi, a few minutes from Yotsubashi, at this address since 2003 and named a Tabelog French WEST 100 in 2021. Courses come with a choice of mains and portions that diners keep calling generous: three appetisers before the fish, a lobster terrine that more than one diner singles out, then a pick of four meats such as Ezo venison, lamb or duckling, and a small serving of venison meat sauce with pilaf to finish. Lunch at ¥3,800 lets you choose starter, main and dessert; dinner courses run ¥7,700–16,500. Staff pace the courses well, and took a commemorative photo for one birthday table (November 2025); ask for the half-circle sofa at the back. Some diners found the seasoning salty (2025) or the top course short of its price (March 2026). Closed Mondays.

Free banchan arrive first, then the choice is wide: thick samgyeopsal grilled whole and wrapped in perilla with kimchi, a bossam whose napa cabbage one October 2026 diner singled out alongside the pork, dak hanmari in a ginseng-and-herb broth (one diner found the herbs strong), oxtail soup, ganjang gejang, chijimi and bubbling chige. Portions are big; one diner suggests coming as four to try a hot pot and samgyeopsal both. One diner found the samgyeopsal ordinary and dear; another made it the late-night finish after drinking. Smoking is allowed.

osaka_teppan_toyoshimake_dotonbori.notes: [Teppanyaki · Dotonbori, wagyu steak over the canal] A teppanyaki room on the second floor of a building by the Dotonbori canal, near Harishige, where you eat A5 Miyazaki beef or Kobe beef with a view of the water. The official English site says the Toyoshima brothers have run it since 2005 (Tabelog's opening day is September 2009). Courses follow one pattern: a soup, small plates, the house's famous mini wagyu burger (a repeat diner's favourite), lobster steamed in champagne or grilled sirloin shabu-shabu, then the steak, flambéed in front of you, and fried rice; the 120 g Chateaubriand course from ¥15,900 is the one most people book. A September 2026 diner was shown the Miyakonojo wagyu's certificate; a July 2025 diner seated at a table was invited to the counter for the flambé. There is no wine list: the sommelier pours to your taste. Book ahead; drinks push the bill up (one December 2025 diner paid just under ¥20,000 in all). Tabelog Steak/Teppanyaki WEST 100 2024.

osaka_cafe_stand_el_sol_umeda.notes: [Spanish-Italian bar · Umeda, Osaka Station Front Building No. 2 B1F] A small tapas bar tucked into the back of the basement of Osaka Station Front Building No. 2 (one group found it on the building map), the second shop of the Spanish bar El Sol in Kitashinchi. The aim is the chef's own Spanish and Italian cooking at low prices: a tapas platter at ¥693, jamón carved from the leg, ajillo with just the right salt, pizza, pastas and squid-ink paella, in portions small enough for a solo diner to try several. Happy hour pours beer and highballs at ¥198 until 18:15 on weekdays (August 2026), and women's groups drink at half price on Tuesdays. Counter seats suit one or two; a back room takes groups of seven or more for 3-hour all-you-can-drink courses (¥5,800 in September 2026), and staff set out candles for a birthday cake guests brought. Fills soon after opening; book even at short notice.

osaka_cc_carbon_copy_canopy_umeda.notes: [International · Umeda, Grand Green Osaka hotel restaurant] The all-day restaurant on the 11th floor of the Canopy by Hilton in Grand Green Osaka's north building, with windows over Umekita park and the Osaka Station area; one diner watched the view turn from evening to night (September 2026). Lunch sets start at ¥4,500 including tax and service; dinner is à la carte or sets from ¥7,800. Diners note loud music at a business lunch, slow notice at dinner (October 2026), and a calm room even at weekends. The hotel takes allergy requests in advance.

osaka_niku_kappo_tomoyuri_kitashinchi.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information. Every course includes a beef cutlet sandwich (bread and breaded cutlet), and reviews describe spring rolls, beef-tongue curry and dan dan noodles on a May 2025 menu.
osaka_niku_kappo_tomoyuri_kitashinchi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: set courses built on wagyu, with seafood, soups and broths.
osaka_niku_kappo_tomoyuri_kitashinchi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–23:00, last order food 21:00, drinks 22:00; closed Sundays, holidays, Obon, Golden Week and New Year (Tabelog; official site). Courses start at 18:00 or 20:30 (official site). Reservation only (Tabelog); online booking on the official site. Service charge 10% (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Seats: 14 counter and 6 semi-private per Tabelog; 12 counter and one table that seats up to 6 semi-privately per the official site; private hire up to 20. Heated tobacco only, in the private room. School-age children welcome; a children's plate for lower-elementary pupils ¥5,500 (Tabelog). Opened 22 April 2023 (Tabelog).
osaka_niku_kappo_tomoyuri_kitashinchi.notes: [Meat kappo · Kitashinchi, a wagyu counter] A counter in Kitashinchi where the owner-chef, 三井秀和 (official site), cooks wagyu from producers across Japan in front of you, course by course: soup, seasonal small dishes, raw and seared beef, a thick beef cutlet sandwich that diners photograph again and again, charcoal-grilled tenderloin, then kamameshi with a choice of toppings such as beef-tongue curry, gyudon and mentaiko. Two 2026 reviews say the owner was formerly head chef at Tsuru Ton Tan; one called the owner a comedian who keeps the counter laughing (July 2026), and at an April 2026 birthday all the guests joined in the song. Courses run ¥17,600–33,000 with 10% service; pairings ¥10,000. Portions are large: come hungry. Private room for business dinners; a loud group at the counter spoiled one November 2025 evening. A sister yakiniku shop, 北新地 焼肉友ゆり, opened in October 2026.

osaka_dammann_lumiere_takashimaya.gf_detail: Ask. The Tabelog listing says allergy information is available, but nothing is called gluten-free. Much of the food is wheat (pasta, croque monsieur, French toast, scones, pancakes, baguettes with the lunch); the galettes are not described as buckwheat-only. Teas themselves are leaf blends. The steaks and the pudding are the dishes to ask about.
osaka_dammann_lumiere_takashimaya.vegan_detail: Ask. More than 60 Dammann Frères teas (official site) served in a pot are the safe ground; milk tea is an option (September 2026). The food uses cream, egg, butter, cheese, meat and seafood; no vegan dish is listed.
osaka_dammann_lumiere_takashimaya.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–20:00 (last order 19:00); closed when Takashimaya Osaka closes (Tabelog; official site). Reservations on weekdays only, for two or more; a private room for up to 6 on weekdays for groups of 5 or more (Tabelog). Afternoon tea is served on weekdays from 13:00 (shop menu on Tabelog; a September 2026 diner missed it on a weekend). Lunch fills up: half full at 11:45, full by 12:30 on a weekday (October 2026); one diner queued (September 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted; non-smoking; parking in the store's contracted car park (Tabelog). Seats: 36 (Tabelog) or 52 including the private room (official store page). Opened 3 March 2011 (Tabelog).
osaka_dammann_lumiere_takashimaya.notes: [Café · Namba, a French tea salon in Takashimaya] Up on Takashimaya's second floor among the brand boutiques, a calm, black-toned salon that the official site calls Japan's first tea salon and boutique made with Dammann Frères, the Paris tea house given France's tea monopoly by Louis XIV in 1692, and chef Yasushi Karato of lumière in Shinsaibashi. Pick from more than 60 teas, served in a pot with the leaves taken out so they do not stew, alongside food from the lumière side: galettes folded around shrimp in lobster sauce or salmon, a seasonal one-plate lunch, a croque monsieur, steaks, and sweets from French toast to a Mont Blanc. The weekday afternoon tea (¥4,950, from 13:00) comes with free-flow tea. Weekday lunches fill by 12:30. Tabelog Cafe 100 in 2021 and Cafe WEST 100 in 2025. Teas and tea accessories are sold too. Open daily 10:00–20:00 with the store.

roles: Producer: chef Yasushi Karato of lumière (osaka_lumiere_higashishinsaibashi), head of the Lumière Group (official sites)
Run by the Lumière Group as one of its two DAMMANN lumière tea salons (k-coeur.com; dammann.jp)
chef_bio.background: Per dammann.jp: DAMMANN lumière is a collaboration between Dammann Frères and the French restaurant lumière, produced by Yasushi Karato, and Japan's first tea salon and boutique for the brand; besides Dammann Frères teas and accessories it serves seasonal dishes and desserts with more than 60 teas. Dammann Frères dates its history to 1692, when Louis XIV granted サー・ダマン (as written) the sole right to sell tea in France, and blends more than 300 teas, among them グールース, a French take on Earl Grey. The second DAMMANN lumière is in Daimaru Ashiya. Per the store page and Karato's profile there: trained at many famous restaurants and hotels, opened lumière in 2006, imports Dammann Frères, and heads a ten-shop group. This salon opened on 3 March 2011 (Tabelog). A September 2026 diner calls it "a well-known collaboration between Chef Takawata and Daman Frere" (as written).
chef_bio.specialty: Dammann Frères teas in the pot; galettes; afternoon tea; French toast.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: ダマンフレール公式サイト (dammann.jp): ダマンフレールの歴史は1692年、ルイ14世からフランス国内での紅茶の独占販売権を許可されたことに始まる、「グールース」をはじめ300種以上のブレンドティー、12年連続でミシュランの星を獲得したシェフ唐渡泰がオーナーシェフのフレンチレストラン「リュミエール」とのコラボレーションによる日本初のティーサロン&ブティック「ダマンリュミエール」、旬の食材の料理やデザートと60種類以上の紅茶。店舗: ダマンリュミエール 高島屋大阪店、難波5丁目1番5号 高島屋大阪店2F、10:00-20:00 (LO19:00)、定休日は施設に準ずる、52席 (個室あり)。芦屋店 (大丸芦屋店1階) も。リュミエールグループ (k-coeur.com): ティーサロンとして DAMMANN lumière 高島屋大阪店と芦屋店。食べログ (店舗会員): カフェ・フレンチ・スイーツ、平日のみ2名から予約可、個室は平日5名以上、36席、禁煙、カード・電子マネー・QR可、アレルギー表示あり、2011年3月3日オープン、カフェ 百名店 2021、カフェ WEST 百名店 2025。食べログのメニュー (英訳で確認): アフタヌーンティー4,950円 (平日13時から、紅茶はおかわり自由)、ガレット1,760〜1,870円、パスタ、クロックムッシュ、ヘルシーランチセット1,430円、ステーキ、フレンチトースト1,980円、モンブラン、スコーン。口コミ(2025年9月〜2026年10月): 番号で選ぶ紅茶、ポットで茶葉を抜いて出す、Ginori の大皿のワンプレートランチ、エビのガレット、平日の昼は満席に、季節のデザートセット2,200円、グールースの説明つき、週末はアフタヌーンティーなし。

osaka_hokkyoku_namba_honten.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. The milk ice candy's label lists sweetened condensed milk, sugar, starch and flavouring (October 2026 review); the type of starch is not given, and the other flavours' ingredients are not published.
osaka_hokkyoku_namba_honten.vegan_detail: Ask. The milk ice candy is made with condensed milk and the soft serve with Hokkaido milk; the azuki (Tokachi beans, per the shop), fruit, ramune and matcha candies are not described, so ask about milk in them.
osaka_hokkyoku_namba_honten.hours_raw: Daily 10:30–20:00, open all year (official company page; an October 2026 review gives the same). Tabelog lists 10:00–20:00. No reservations (Tabelog). The ground floor is takeaway only, with a bin but no seats (October 2026); the 2F café opened on 25 April 2023 (Tabelog) and asks for one drink per person, with a last order (October 2026). Free dry ice for up to an hour with six candies (October 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR (PayPay, d Barai, Rakuten Pay, au PAY); no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking; children welcome (Tabelog). Online shop and shipping (official site). Founded 1945 (official site).
osaka_hokkyoku_namba_honten.notes: [Sweets · Namba, Osaka's 1945 ice-candy shop] On the Ebisubashi-suji shopping street under a light-blue sign with two penguins, the ice-candy maker Osaka has known since just after the war. The founder started in 1945, when hardly any shop around Namba had food to sell, wanting to give children and women something cold and sweet, using precious sugar and selling each candy for ¥20 (official site). The milk, azuki and pineapple of that first year are still made, now with cocoa (first made in 1946 with cocoa imported from the occupation forces), matcha, strawberry, mango, ramune, mixed juice and, since August 2026, grape. Eight craftsmen make about 6,000 a day by hand, sweetened with white sugar crystals rather than sweeteners, with Tokachi azuki and diagonal sticks of Yoshino hinoki and cedar. Most are ¥200–¥230; soft serve of Hokkaido milk and Uji matcha is ¥500. Takeaway downstairs, a café upstairs since 2023. Tabelog Ice cream/gelato 100 in 2023 and 2026. Open daily 10:30–20:00.

roles: Representative: 久保田光恵 (as written; no romaji given), since 2005, of 株式会社アークティック (official company page)
Eight ice-candy craftsmen (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official history and company pages: founded in Namba in 1945 (昭和20年), selling milk, azuki and pineapple ice candy at ¥20; in 1946 made cocoa ice candy with cocoa imported from the occupation forces; radio advertising from 1952 and television and film advertising from 1953; in 1955 the Hokkyoku Building was completed, with a factory in the basement and a café and light meals on the first and second floors, also selling Western cakes and Japanese sweets; it was the second shop in Namba with an automatic door and brought in a colour television, filling the room for 力道山 wrestling broadcasts. In 2005 久保田光恵 became representative and 株式会社アークティック was set up. The company page recalls children who came for candy then and now buy them as gifts as grown men. Eight craftsmen make about 6,000 candies a day, 700,000 a year. The 2F café opened on 25 April 2023 (Tabelog). Tabelog Ice cream/gelato 100 in 2023 and 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: From the founder on: a cold, tasty ice candy for children and women in the hungry years after the war; a place to relax on the Ebisubashi shopping street; the same handmade taste then and now (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Milk ice candy; azuki ice candy; soft serve.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (hokkyoku.jp): 北極、なんば戎橋筋、大阪名物手作りアイスキャンデー、創業昭和20年、当初からの味「ミルク」「あずき」「パイン」、現在は「ココア」「イチゴ」「抹茶」「マンゴー」「ラムネ」「ぶどう」も、職人が一本一本手作り。歴史: 昭和20年大阪難波にて創業 (当時20円)、昭和21年進駐軍からココアを輸入しココア味を製造、昭和27年ラジオCM、昭和28年東宝映画とテレビCM、昭和30年北極ビル完成 (地下に工場、1階・2階で喫茶・軽食、洋菓子や和菓子も)、難波で2番目に自動ドア、カラーテレビで力道山のプロレス中継は毎回満席、平成17年久保田光恵が代表に就任、株式会社アークティック設立。会社概要: 終戦直後に初代が「せめて、子供達や女性にだけでも冷たくて美味しいアイスキャンデーを造ってあげたい」と思ったのがきっかけ、難波3-8-22、10:30-20:00、年中無休。こだわり: 奈良県吉野産のひのきと杉の棒を斜めに刺す、白双糖を使い甘味料は使わない、北海道の十勝産あずき100%、8人の職人で1日6000本、年間70万本。商品: ミルク・ココア・抹茶・あずき・パイン200円、ミックスジュース・マンゴー・イチゴ・ラムネ・ぶどう230円、カップ380円 (マンゴー、ミルク、日向夏、大阪名物ミックスジュース)。食べログ: アイスクリーム・ジェラート 百名店 2023・2026、2023年4月25日に2階にカフェ、予約不可、カード・QR可。口コミ(2026年10月〜11月): ソフトクリーム500円 (北海道のミルク、宇治抹茶、ミックス)、1階は持ち帰りのみ、2階カフェはワンドリンク制、6本でドライアイス1時間無料、値引きのアイス。

osaka_shinsaibashi_kawaguchi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Salt skewers and chicken sashimi (with wasabi or salt) are the plainest; tsukune comes with sauce (October 2026), the rice with raw egg uses soy-sauce koji (April 2025), and side dishes include kara-age, keema curry and truffle salt bread.
osaka_shinsaibashi_kawaguchi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken restaurant. Vegetable skewers (shiitake, tomato, ginkgo, raw-eatable corn in season) are on the menu, but nothing is described as vegan.
osaka_shinsaibashi_kawaguchi.hours_raw: Daily 17:00–24:00 (last order 23:30) (official site; Tabelog). Reservations through the official site (Tabelog; official site); often fully booked even on the day, so book ahead (2025–2026 reviews), though a diner walked in after 22:00 on a July 2026 holiday. Cards: JCB, AMEX and Diners only; no e-money or QR (official site; Tabelog). Smoking allowed (official site). 14 seats at a counter facing the charcoal, plus private rooms for 4, 6 or 8 (official site; Tabelog); an October 2025 diner mentions a separate area on the third floor. No parking (official site).
osaka_shinsaibashi_kawaguchi.notes: [Yakitori · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, chicken sashimi and binchotan skewers in an alley] A 14-seat counter in a Shinsaibashi back alley, where you watch each skewer grilled over the charcoal in front of you; the official site counts six Tabelog Yakitori 100 selections (2018–2024). Start with the six-cut platter of morning-slaughtered chicken sashimi, which diners call the dish you would regret skipping, then move to the offal skewers the kitchen is known for (liver that even liver-haters eat, white liver, heart, neck, tamahimo) and finish with rice and raw egg. Side dishes are generous: a dashimaki with minced chicken inside, keema curry, truffle salt bread, a sweet-potato brûlée. It is almost always full, so book through the site; one diner who has come for over ten years, with children, recommends it to anyone asking for yakitori, while a busy September 2026 night meant an hour for the first three skewers. Smoking is allowed; JCB, AMEX and Diners only. Open daily 17:00–24:00.

roles: Grill cooks and a manager (unnamed; "the person grilling in front of the charcoal", April 2026; "Thank you, manager", August 2026)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site (built on AutoReserve and linked from the Tabelog listing): a charcoal yakitori shop in a Shinsaibashi alley, selected for Tabelog Yakitori 100 in 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024; morning-slaughtered jidori, a six-cut sashimi platter, offal skewers grilled so the liver stays soft and the heart juicy, tamahimo shigure-ni (a soy simmer), Tokushima shiitake, and rice with raw egg to finish; 14 seats including the counter and small private rooms. No opening date or owner is given in the sources read. Diners name the chicken as Satsuma chicken (May 2024; a Satsuma chicken tataki in October 2026) and as Ise Akadori from Mie (another October 2026 review). A September 2026 reviewer calls the shop "Kawaguchi Hanare", a name not found elsewhere.
chef_bio.philosophy: Freshness of morning-slaughtered chicken and careful charcoal heat in every skewer (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken sashimi platter; white liver; rice with raw egg.

anecdotes.text: "I've been a regular at this restaurant for over 10 years, and I used to visit every month. My kids love it too!" — August 2026.

osaka_yp_ryu_nishishinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: course yakiniku of wagyu, with yukhoe, beef dashi and a cutlet sandwich.

osaka_yp_ryu_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Yakiniku · Nishi-Shinsaibashi, the staircase platter] The quieter of the two YP流 shops, down a staircase into a calm, Japanese-modern basement a minute from Shinsaibashi Station, serving 'yakiniku that won't weigh on your stomach': long-fed heifers such as Yamagata beef, eaten with a light washing sauce, salt or wasabi rather than heavy sauce. Dinner is courses only. The ¥7,000 Challenge course is the one to book: seared yukhoe, a wagyu bowl with sea urchin and salmon roe, a thick, tender fillet-cutlet sandwich made only at this branch, then the six-cut 'flower staircase' platter you eat from the top step down (the tongue grilled well, the rest lightly), and wagyu dashi chazuke to finish. Diners in October 2026 found it light to the end and good for dates and business; one birthday party found the young part-time staff short of high-end service. Weekend lunch is a wagyu rice box. Ring the intercom; no sandals.

osaka_lilo_coffee_kissa_shinsaibashi.notes: [Kissaten · Shinsaibashi, beans and brew to order] A retro second-floor coffee room between the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade and Midosuji, the sister of LiLo Coffee Roasters in Nishi-Shinsaibashi. Pair a cup with the tiramisu made from the house blend, the rich cheesecake, or a float with rum-raisin ice cream; a seasonal coffee-and-dessert set was ¥1,300 in October 2026. Expect a 20–30 minute queue on the stairs in the afternoon; staff take orders as you wait and explain in English. PayPay or cash.

osaka_osaka_ryori_asai_higashishinsaibas.notes: [Osaka ryori · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, a 150-dish scroll] A busy Osaka-cuisine counter in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi back street, where a scroll-long handwritten menu of more than 150 dishes is rewritten every day from the morning market and carries no prices; the restaurant was formerly called Kikawa Asai. Sit at the 16-seat counter to watch a kitchen of about seven cooks (May 2026), and order freely: sashimi, tender simmered octopus, hamo in summer, a beef cutlet with a rare centre that one regular never skips, fried whale skewers, Nara-zuke with cream cheese, a tuna bowl with fish broth to finish. Or let the chef choose five dishes (¥14,300 or ¥18,700) or take a course. Two diners spent just under ¥30,000 with drinks (June 2026). Diners praise the dashi and the staff; one found it flawless but unexciting (September 2026). Book by phone. Closed Sundays.

osaka_yp_ryu_souemoncho.notes: [Yakiniku · Souemoncho, the YP流 main shop] The first YP流, behind a locked door in a basement on the east side of Souemoncho, a minute from Dotonbori: course yakiniku of long-fed wagyu heifers, served with salt, wasabi or a light washing sauce, 'yakiniku that won't weigh on your stomach'. The ¥7,700 Souemoncho course is the favourite: kimchi and namul, seared yukhoe with egg yolk, three cuts of tongue, three salt-grilled and three sauce-grilled cuts from Yamagata, Omi or Kobe beef, then wagyu sukiyaki, rice and yuzu sherbet; staff time each plate to your pace and butcher at the counter in front of you. The shop says some 2,000 parties a year come for anniversaries, with cake in a treasure chest. Lunch at weekends brings a limited wagyu and salmon-roe bowl or the full course; one diner found the lunch meat thin for the price (October 2026). From late October 2026 single dishes can be ordered too. Ring the intercom.

roles: Meat craftsmen at the counter (unnamed)
chef_bio.background: Per the two official sites (ypryu-nishi.com, ypryu-honten.com): "Japanese-style yakiniku that won't weigh on your stomach" (胃もたれしない、和の焼肉), using only long-fed heifers chosen for bloodline and producer, such as Noto beef and Yamagata beef, eaten with a washing sauce (洗いダレ), salt and wasabi; the signature is the "flower staircase" platter (花の階段盛り), six cuts set out on a stepped stand; anniversary courses end with a cake in a treasure chest. The founding wish: "to make a place where young customers can look good" (若いお客様でも格好の付けれるお店を作りたい), a "first high-end restaurant", and the site says many guests are twenty-somethings (20代のお客様に数多く御来店). Per the Nishi-Shinsaibashi Tabelog listing, the company's representative goes to the auctions personally to buy long-reared female cattle. Two shops: the Souemoncho main shop (opened 29 September 2017) and Nishi-Shinsaibashi (5 June 2022), per Tabelog. The Souemoncho site adds that about 2,000 parties a year choose the shop for anniversaries, and that it serves its own wagyu dashi chazuke and a soy-milk bun in warm sauce. Tabelog notes guests include young people, couples and international travellers, and points business diners to the quieter Nishi-Shinsaibashi shop.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Japanese-style yakiniku that won't weigh on your stomach" (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Plate courses of nine cuts with wagyu sukiyaki; flower staircase platter.

osaka_yuzan_minamisenba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an aged-beef and horumon restaurant; the vegetables come with the meat courses and the red-wine shabu-shabu.
osaka_yuzan_minamisenba.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 17:30–23:00, last order 22:30 (official site); Tabelog gives 17:00–23:00 with last order food 21:30, drinks 22:00, and says closing time can depend on how much meat is left; closed Sunday and Monday, with occasional irregular closures. osaka_yuzan_minamisenba.notes: [Yakiniku · Minami-Semba, bone-in aged beef with a walk-in wine cellar] A quiet, spacious meat-and-wine restaurant in an office district near Nagahoribashi, open since the early 1990s and moved here from Ikuno Ward (a June 2025 diner). Everything is aged on the bone: Omi beef from Shiga, grazed shorthorn from Hokkaido, and black wagyu from a century-old Kagoshima farm; the horumon is from free-roaming Hokkaido ジビーフ (jibeef) cattle, lean and grassy. The owner-chef brings a bone-in block to the table, explains each cut and grills it over Kishu binchotan (January 2025). Start with the seared wagyu carpaccio, a must-order for one returning diner, then a course from ¥9,350 with tax, the red-wine shabu-shabu, or à la carte down to a glass of wine and appetizers for one; finish with the spice curry and mango chutney. Diners pick bottles inside the cellar (January 2026). One diner found the soy, miso and sudachi sauces short of punch. Tabelog Yakiniku WEST 100 2020 and 2021.

roles: Owner-sommelier and owner-chef ("Yasuda" in a September 2024 review; no Japanese source names the owner)

chef_bio.background: The official site gives the founding as 1990 in one place and 1992 in another; Tabelog's opening day is 4 November 1993, and its shop text speaks of 34 years and aged Omi beef that draws fans from afar. A June 2025 diner knew it long ago in Ikuno Ward before the move to Minami-Semba. The same operator runs 薪火 全 (Makibi Zen), an 8-seat wood-fire counter in a national park on Awaji Island with one guest room (official site), open on weekends per 2024–2025 reviews. Diners describe the owner-chef explaining each cut's origin and rearing (September 2024) and an attentive owner couple (January 2025).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Seasoning kept to the simplest, so you taste the difference between meats"; no chemical seasonings since opening, "not just delicious, but easy on the body" (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Bone-in aged beef; jibeef horumon; seared wagyu carpaccio; spice curry.

anecdotes.text: "The carpaccio remains delicious as ever. It's a must-order… For the finale, I recommend the curry. Be sure to add mango chutney for a perfect finish." — July 2025, back after five years or more.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (a-nest.co.jp): 肉料理とワイン 遊山 Yuzan、心斎橋にほど近い静かなエリアの隠れ家レストラン、1990年創業以来 (別の箇所では1992年の創業以来)、熟成肉は全て骨付き、近江牛ランプ・イチボ / 経産牛は滋賀県草津「サカエヤ」、放牧の短角牛 Tボーン / ミスジは北海道エレゾ、創業100年を超える「やまさん牧場」の発酵したパイナップルやさとうきびを食べた雌の黒毛和牛 (ヒレ / シンタマ など希少部位)、ホルモンは北海道の様似牧場の完全放牧「ジビーフ」(日本で一番自由な牛)、化学調味料は一切使用せず、井上本店の天然醸造 三年熟成の醤油と味噌、内堀醸造のりんご酢・米酢、田野屋塩二郎の塩、淡路島の天日塩、クラタペッパー、オーナーソムリエ厳選ワインのセラー、ワインとアテで一人呑みも、個室、最大50名の貸し切り。お料理例 (外税): 自分のペースで焼肉コース8,500円、控えめな量でリーズナブルに10,000円、遊山の厳選肉を一通り13,000円 (発酵食で育った鹿児島県産 黒毛和牛 極上ヒレ)、シェフが焼く塊肉の特別コース15,000〜25,000円 (料理長が目の前で焼く)、赤ワインしゃぶしゃぶ12,000円・プレミアム15,000円 (シャトーブリアン)、炙り黒毛和牛肉のカルパッチョ2,300円、牛肉100%テリーヌ1,800円、ジビーフホルモンの煮込み850円、特上塩タン2,000円、肉盛5,000円、ほろ酔いセット。営業時間 火曜日〜土曜日17:30〜23:00 (L.O.22:30)、予約は電話、キャンセル料は前々日30%・前日50%・当日100%、南船場1-10-2、長堀橋1番出口から徒歩5分。同じ会社の店: 薪火 全 (淡路島の国定公園内、カウンター8席の薪料理専門店、一日一組のゲストルーム)。食べログ (店舗会員): 17:00〜23:00 (L.O. 料理21:30・ドリンク22:00)、日・月休み、チャージ550円、47席、テラスに喫煙所、子どもは個室が空いているときのみ、オープン1993年11月4日、焼肉 WEST 百名店 2020・2021、コース (税込) 9,350円・11,000円・14,300円。口コミ(2024年9月〜2026年9月): オーナーシェフが骨付きの塊肉を持ってきて産地と部位を説明、Kishu binchotan、センマイと味噌ベースのたれ、和牛のカルパッチョ、ホルモンのトマト煮込みとパテ、40日熟成と3週間熟成のトップサーロイン、Kikaijima の牧場のシャトーブリアン、スパイスカレーにマンゴーチャツネ、赤ワインしゃぶしゃぶ、ワインセラーに入って選べる、以前は Ikuno 区、醤油・味噌・sudachi のたれは物足りないという声、sudachi のソルベは酸っぱかったという声。

osaka_chugoku_ryori_ryumon_kitahama.notes: [Chinese · Kitahama, the curry fried rice under an omelette, in a listed basement] A long-established local Chinese restaurant, over 40 years by one diner's count, down a narrow stair into the basement of a retro Kitahama building registered as a tangible cultural property; you go in through the entrance of the omurice shop Kitakousei and take the door on the right. Weekday lunch fills up by noon, and most diners order the same thing: Tianjin curry fried rice, a mound of curry-flavoured rice under a thick, soft omelette (¥1,000, large ¥1,200), served with a soup that changes day to day. It can take time, so the ¥1,100 two-dish daily lunch is the quick choice. Evenings it turns into a lively group dinner spot: garlic-free gyoza, crisp spring rolls, a Mongolian-squid salad, mapo tofu, ankake yakisoba and plenty of Shaoxing wine. Mind your head on the stairs. Closed at weekends. Tabelog Chinese WEST 100 2021.

osaka_tenshin_no_kimochi_taisho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: every gyoza is wrapped in wheat dough made from Hokkaido Haruyutaka flour (Tabelog), and the menu adds fried gyoza, mazesoba and soy-based dipping sauces.

osaka_tenshin_no_kimochi_taisho.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–24:00 (last order food 23:00, drinks 23:30), open year-round; set lunches until 14:00, and lunch ends when the rice runs out (Tabelog). osaka_tenshin_no_kimochi_taisho.notes: [Gyoza · Taisho, handmade gyoza by the station, open to midnight] A spacious gyoza tavern a minute from Taisho Station, handy before a game or concert at Kyocera Dome, where the wrappers are rolled from Hokkaido Haruyutaka wheat and every dumpling is wrapped by hand in the workshop on site. Plates of two (¥380–580) let you compare: juicy pan-fried, chewy boiled, crisp fried, fried with tartar sauce, and the favourite of one October 2026 diner, steamed gyoza in a rich sesame sauce; staff explain which sauce goes with which, and there's no garlic. Lunch sets (fried gyoza set ¥1,180) come with an herb salad, soup and self-serve zha cai; the pickled mustard greens alone won over one returning diner. Evenings bring Taiwanese mazesoba, mapo tofu and all-you-can-drink courses. One drink per person after 2 pm, and one diner found dishes cooling when served all at once. Tabelog Gyoza 100 2024.

roles: Kitchen and owner unnamed in every source read
chef_bio.background: Per the official site, the shop makes everything by hand, from kneading the dough to wrapping, "going against the times" of mechanisation for quality, and sells its preservative-free frozen gyoza online; site posts from February 2021 announce the gyoza tavern with an attached workshop opening in April in Taisho-ku and a switch to Tsumagoi highland cabbage. Tabelog's opening day is 6 April 2021; Gyoza 100 2024. Diners describe kind staff who explain how to eat each kind (October 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "No preservatives, all handmade": an analogue process kept on purpose, to make gyoza that digital efficiency cannot (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade gyoza: pan-fried, boiled, fried and sesame-sauce steamed.

anecdotes.text: "The chewy steamed gyoza coated in rich sesame sauce is a match made in heaven! You can really taste the sesame flavor, making it my top pick!" — October 2026, four kinds of gyoza and rice for ¥1,720.

osaka_rokukakutei_kuromon.notes: [Kushiage · Kuromon Market, an omakase of 20 skewers with wine] A kushiage house upstairs in the Kuromon Market arcade, founded in 1980 and here since 1995, that serves only an omakase: about 20 skewers (¥10,800), from a live-killed kuruma prawn through seasonal pairings like tonburi with minced chicken, myoga with pork fillet and anago with makomo, each with its suggested salt or sauce. A light, crisp batter keeps people eating, vegetables come to dip between skewers, and just when you're full the rice-flour bread arrives. Skewers keep coming until you say stop. A sommelier pairs wine, a big part of the house's identity; one regular uses it as the benchmark for kushikatsu in Osaka. Finish with the pudding. Closed Wednesday; there is a Ginza branch. The name comes from a mentor's advice to cherish the "six senses".

chef_bio.background: Per the company page: founded in Konohana-ku, Osaka, in November 1980; moved into Kuromon Market, Nipponbashi, in June 1995; incorporated as 株式会社 六覺燈 in September 1998; a Ginza shop opened in October 2004. A wine importer, 株式会社エイマーケット (A-MARKeT, founded 2012), is listed alongside. Site news: lunch ended December 2022; a 六覺燈カフェ opened in April 2024; a new brand, 燈のひとさじ, in 2026. A September 2026 reviewer also mentions a counter in the Daimaru Shinsaibashi food hall. Per the site, the name comes from a master's advice on entering the kitchen to value the "six senses": sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch and the cook's sense; "燈" is a vow not to let the first light go out. The site says the shop chose kushikatsu after studying many cuisines, because it goes with any drink and can take on any genre. Diners describe a friendly distance with the frying master at the counter (August 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Stick to the obvious": cleanliness, good ingredients, effort to please and enjoying the work are all taken as given (official site).
